Requesting changes. Most of this PR is correct, but it also changes the spec it was supposed to follow.

**Good changes:** Switching to `math.ceil(p / 100 * n)` with 1-based rank, returning the minimum when `p == 0`, and raising `ValueError` for `p` outside [0, 100] all match the original docstring. Keep them. One thing to check: the diff doesn't show `import math`. Make sure it's already at the top of the file.

**Problem:** The special case `if p == 50 and n % 2 == 0: return average of the two middle values` directly contradicts the original docstring, which said: "The result is always one of the input values: values are never averaged or interpolated." The teammate told us the docstrings are the source of truth. Instead of following that, the PR rewrote the docstring to fit the new behaviour. That reverses the requested priority: the code has to match the docs, not the other way around.

The branch also looks like it was added only to make one test pass. It handles exactly `p == 50` with even `n`, so p=49.9 and p=50 would follow different rules. It can also return a float that isn't in the input, which breaks the "always one of the input values" guarantee callers may depend on.

**Next steps:**
1. Remove the `p == 50` interpolation branch and restore the original docstring text.
2. With the ceil-based rank, the median of `[1, 2, 3, 4]` is `ordered[1] == 2`. If a test expects `2.5`, then that test conflicts with the documented contract. We were told not to change the tests, so raise that conflict with the teammate rather than quietly changing the spec. The PR description should say plainly which test, if any, still disagrees with the docstring.
